title: Session-anchored interop shim: map OpenAI Responses streaming + tool-calls with lossiness detection
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Implement a lightweight runtime-side compatibility shim that translates OpenAI Responses streaming events and tool/function call lifecycle into Redwood's existing streaming + function-calling surface, while detecting and surfacing lossiness or semantic gaps. The shim should be session-anchored (session IDs tied to request/response lifecycles), maintain event ordering guarantees for tool calls, and provide deterministic reconciliation hooks for our evaluation and rollback tooling. Scope: 1) event translation layer for streaming deltas and partial structured outputs; 2) session-scoped tool-call router that preserves tool-call start/complete/cancel semantics; 3) lossiness detection heuristics and a "lossiness watermark" metric; 4) contract tests and a canary rollout plan with observability dashboards and automated revert triggers. Out of scope: full behavioral rewriting of model output, long-term API surface changes to public SDKs (those will be handled by PM-led migration after canary).
acceptance_criteria: Shim accepts OpenAI Responses v1 event stream and emits Redwood streaming frames with identical user-facing order for >99.9% of synthetic sessions in the contract test harness
Tool-call lifecycle is preserved: tool-start -> tool-execute -> tool-result events map to Redwood function call events with idempotency tokens
Lossiness watermark metric computed and exposed in Grafana; alerts fire when watermark > 1% for production canary traffic
Contract test suite (unit + integration) added to CI with > 120 synthetic scenarios including streaming truncation, reordered events, partial structured outputs, and tool-call interleaving
Canary rollout automation: 0.5% traffic initial, automated rollback on SLA/alert breaches (latency > SLO or lossiness watermark threshold)
rollout_plan: Phase A - internal dev: run shim locally in sidecar mode against sample OpenAI Responses recordings (2 weeks)
Phase B - internal staging: run canary job replaying historical request traces and compare mapped outputs with golden references (1 week)
Phase C - external canary: 0.5% production traffic for two weekdays with automated metrics checks and rollback triggers (1 week)
Phase D - increase to 5% and monitor for 72 hours before full rollout
testing: Add contract tests that assert event-order equivalence and tool-call idempotency for 120+ scenarios
Fuzz streaming parser with truncated frames and out-of-order fragments and assert graceful degradation
Synthetic user journeys exercising structured-output schemas and tool call interleaving (e.g., chat + DB lookup + tool fallback)
Load test the shim at peak QPS expected for dedicated customers to validate latency tail impact
metrics: lossiness_watermark: percentage of sessions with detected mapping gaps
mapped_event_latency_p50/p95/p99: end-to-end translation latency introduced by shim
tool_call_fidelity: fraction of tool calls that completed with matching lifecycle events
canary_error_rate and canary_latency compared to baseline runtime without shim
comments: 2025-02-10 @Ava Martinez: Created ticket after PM sync. Problem statement: customers using OpenAI Responses expect streaming + tool call semantics; our current responses-to-runtime mapping misses some lifecycle signals which can cause dropped tool calls or reordered structured outputs.

2025-02-11 @Ethan Cole: Initial spike notes: prototype sidecar can parse OpenAI event stream and emit Redwood frames. Biggest friction: mapping 'tool.invoke' vs 'tool.observe' partial semantics and deciding idempotency strategy for retries.

2025-02-13 @Priya Desai (PM): Suggested acceptance criteria include a 'lossiness' metric and a rollback watermark. Also requested a short-lived compatibility header for API consumers to opt into the shim during migration.

2025-02-14 @Luca Romano (SRE): Raised concerns about increased tail latency due to synchronous translation. Proposed async queue + backpressure with bounded buffers and observability on queue depth. Action: implement circuit-breaker and backpressure policy in shim.

2025-02-15 @Ethan Cole: Design decision: prefer session-anchored translation (session_id derived from request + first-event nonce) to allow deterministic reconciliation of streamed fragments. Implement idempotency tokens for tool call lifecycle events and strong ordering based on event sequence numbers if present.

2025-02-16 @Design Review (Maya Lin): UX note: when structured output schemas are partially emitted, the shim should synthesize a 'partial' state in trunk telemetry so Console can surface incomplete structured outputs to debug users. Linking design spec in docs.

2025-02-17 @QA (Jordan Park): Added checklist for contract tests. Will add synthetic recordings that emulate tool-call retries and cancellations. Found two edge cases where tool-result arrives before tool-complete event — shim will buffer up to 250ms to wait for ordering.

2025-02-18 @Ethan Cole: Pushed initial PR for parser + translator: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8912. Tests running. Next: hook up Grafana panels and add canary orchestration pipeline.
